Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

retain verb

keep, not lose or give up

also keep, hold on to, keep hold of, hang on to, retention, confine, keep in

classical

Cic. Quinct. 59: ut amīcōs observantiā, rem parsimōniā retinēret (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Amic. 70: retinent tamen cāritātem in pāstōrēs

retineō, retinēre, retinuī, retentum

verb, second conjugation, with the accusative

keep, hold on to

Keep what one has: friends, property, a custom, one’s dignity, a sense of proportion. Its first sense is “hold back, detain” (quid mē retinēs?, Plaut. Ep. 1.1.61) and so “restrain” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • teneō, tenēre, tenuī, tentum — hold, keep

    verb, second conjugation, with the accusative · also used · classical · Traupman 336

    The plain verb for holding; memoriā tenēre is “remember”. See hold on.

  • contineō, continēre, continuī, contentum — keep in, confine

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 336

Examples

  • ut amīcōs observantiā, rem parsimōniā retinēret

    to keep his friends by attentiveness and his property by thriftCic. Quinct. 59 (Lewis & Short)

  • lūdendī etiam est quīdam modus retinendus

    even in play a certain limit must be keptCic. Off. 1.104

  • cum cognitī sunt et aut deōrum aut rēgum fīliī inventī, retinent tamen cāritātem in pāstōrēs, quōs patrēs multōs annōs esse dūxērunt

    when they have been recognised and found to be sons of gods or kings, they still keep their love for the shepherds they took for their fathers for many yearsCic. Amic. 70

See also maintain, keep, hold on.
